concept_purpose: Deleuze's term (from Cinema 1) for a deconnected, emptied-out cinematic space that detaches affect from sensory-motor action, describing a postwar crisis of perception
paper_title: Antonioni's cinema of any-space-whatever: Antonioni, posthumanism, material interconnectedness
journal: Studies in European Cinema
paper_argument: Reads Antonioni's modernist landscapes as Deleuzian any-spaces that dissolve the human subject into a field of material relations, reframing his alienation films as ecological visions of human-nonhuman entanglement

concept_purpose: Concept of trans-corporeality and material interconnectedness theorising the porous co-constitution of human bodies and the more-than-human environment
paper_title: Antonioni's cinema of any-space-whatever: Antonioni, posthumanism, material interconnectedness
journal: Studies in European Cinema
paper_argument: Mobilises new-materialist posthumanism (Alaimo, Latour, Morton) to argue that Antonioni's emptied spaces register the Anthropocene entanglement of bodies and matter rather than mere existential malaise

concept_purpose: Object-oriented concept for entities (climate, pollution) massively distributed in time and space that exceed human perception, explaining ecological awareness in the Anthropocene
paper_title: Antonioni's cinema of any-space-whatever: Antonioni, posthumanism, material interconnectedness
journal: Studies in European Cinema
paper_argument: Uses Morton's hyperobjects and ecological thought to read Antonioni's deserts and industrial wastelands as figurations of planetary-scale ecological crisis exceeding the human frame

concept_purpose: Deleuzian conception (Logique du sens; Nietzsche) of the pure event and untimely history that breaks linear chronology to release becoming and counter-actualisation
paper_title: Cinema and history-Event: a Deleuzian perspective on two metafictional historical films depicting Portugal's political history and mythical constructs
journal: Studies in European Cinema
paper_argument: Argues that two Portuguese metafictional historical films enact a Deleuzian 'history-Event' that destabilises national myth and official chronology, opening history to becoming rather than commemoration

concept_purpose: Lyotard's concept for an irresolvable dispute lacking a shared idiom, exposing how dominant discourse silences incommensurable claims
paper_title: Cinema and history-Event: a Deleuzian perspective on two metafictional historical films depicting Portugal's political history and mythical constructs
journal: Studies in European Cinema
paper_argument: Draws on Lyotard's differend alongside Deleuze and Nietzsche to show how the films stage the unrepresentable conflicts of Portugal's colonial and revolutionary past

concept_purpose: Fricker's concept for the wrong done to someone in their capacity as a knower (testimonial and hermeneutical injustice), explaining how marginalised subjects are denied credibility
paper_title: Resisting epistemic injustice: the unknown knowns of the protagonist of Cristi Puiu's Aurora (2010)
journal: Studies in European Cinema
paper_argument: Argues that Puiu's radically unknowable protagonist, via reversed dramatic irony and unbroken long takes, resists the marginalisation produced by epistemic injustice, modelling a survivor's opacity

concept_purpose: Mbembe's theory of sovereignty as the power to dictate who may live and who must die, describing colonial and racialised regimes of disposability
paper_title: Architectures of power and decay: colonial necropolitics and imperial debris in Coup de Torchon/clean slate (Bertrand Tavernier, 1981)
journal: Studies in European Cinema
paper_argument: Reads Tavernier's colonial spaces (latrine, police post, cemetery) as necropolitical sites where authority collapses into abandonment, erasure and racialised disposability rather than stable control

concept_purpose: Stoler's concept of imperial debris and the ongoing processes of ruination through which colonial power persists in degraded material and social forms
paper_title: Architectures of power and decay: colonial necropolitics and imperial debris in Coup de Torchon/clean slate (Bertrand Tavernier, 1981)
journal: Studies in European Cinema
paper_argument: Uses Stoler's imperial debris (with Foucault on disciplinary power) to argue the film stages a spatial politics of ruin in which colonial sovereignty decays into absurdity and violence

concept_purpose: Plumwood's ecofeminist critique of the dualisms (human/nature, reason/body) that license the 'mastery' and othering of the nonhuman
paper_title: Othering nature: an ecocritical reading of Jessica Hausner's Little Joe (2019)
journal: Studies in European Cinema
paper_argument: Applies Plumwood's hegemonic centrism and the plant-horror tradition to argue Little Joe stages anxieties about the human mastery and othering of vegetal nature in an ecological-crisis register

concept_purpose: Critical theorisation of postwar West German philosemitism as a taboo that invests 'the Jew' with a damaging psychosexual power within the German subject
paper_title: Trans misery and Jewish danger: Fassbinder's in einem Jahr mit 13 Monden (in a year of 13 Moons)
journal: Studies in European Cinema
paper_argument: Argues Fassbinder's film attacks philosemitic taboo through erotics, dramatising how the abstraction of Jewishness becomes psychosexually fatal to the postwar German subject while attending to trans suffering

concept_purpose: Reframing women's cinema through agency and companionship rather than the scopophilic/voyeuristic gaze that fixes women as passive objects
paper_title: Glaring and out loud! Thinking women's cinema in Turkey through agency and companionship
journal: Studies in European Cinema
paper_argument: Argues post-2005 women's cinema in Turkey, energised by a rising feminist movement, disrupts dominant narrative codes and scopophilic looking through depictions of female agency and companionship

concept_purpose: Varda's cinecriture and the dialectic of subjective vs objective time used to construct an embodied, wandering female subject against objectifying looking
paper_title: Between Paris and Cleo: soundtrack, temporality and female subjectivity in Cleo from 5 to 7
journal: Studies in European Cinema
paper_argument: Reads Cleo's soundtrack and temporal structure as constructing female subjectivity through sensory wandering and the dialectic of subjective and objective time, countering the silencing of women characters

concept_purpose: Deleuze's concept of the fold (le pli) describing continuous enfolding of matter, body and world without fixed boundaries
paper_title: The heart and the sea: on the lifeblood and elemental folds of Reparer les vivants
journal: French Screen Studies
paper_argument: Uses Deleuze's writings on the fold to argue that Quillevere's heart-transplant film enfolds narrative into elemental bonds of air, water, blood and seawater, theorising an archaic connectivity of the human and the elements

concept_purpose: Genre-critical and affect framework dissecting how the rape-revenge form's final violent sexual acts confound moral and sensory legibility for spectators
paper_title: Anger/sex/genre: de(con)structing rape-revenge in Baise-moi and Descent
journal: French Screen Studies
paper_argument: Argues both films deconstruct rape-revenge conventions by rendering their climactic violence illegible, exposing the genre's entanglement of anger, sex and spectatorial complicity

concept_purpose: The auteur-theory politique des auteurs that canonised directors as the central creative authority, here interrogated for the Tradition of Quality
paper_title: Mise en scene and authorship in the Tradition of Quality (1945-1960)
journal: French Screen Studies
paper_argument: Revisits the politique des auteurs and mise en scene to reassess the maligned Tradition of Quality, arguing for a more nuanced account of authorship and craft in postwar French cinema

concept_purpose: Caillois's taxonomy of play (agon, alea, mimicry, ilinx) used to analyse competing logics of competition and surrender embodied by characters
paper_title: Play and Performance, Perfection and Pessimism: A Reassessment of (the Politics of) Point Break
journal: Journal of Popular Film and Television
paper_argument: Uses Caillois's categories of play to read Point Break as a conflict between agonistic pursuit and ecstatic surrender, yielding a pessimistic verdict on the cynical 'game' of culture-industry entertainment

concept_purpose: Munoz's concepts of queer futurity and queer utopia as a horizon of hope opposed to 'straight time' and pragmatic heteronormative temporality
paper_title: Straight Time and Queer Utopia: Anthony Bridgerton and Kate Sharma's Disorientating Desire in the Regency
journal: Journal of Popular Film and Television
paper_argument: Argues Anthony and Kate's romance momentarily inhabits queer utopia against straight time, but the series reabsorbs them into heteronormative 'happy endings,' stripping their queer potential

concept_purpose: Edelman's anti-social thesis that politics is organised around 'the Child' and reproductive futurity, against which queerness names the death drive
paper_title: Straight Time and Queer Utopia: Anthony Bridgerton and Kate Sharma's Disorientating Desire in the Regency
journal: Journal of Popular Film and Television
paper_argument: Reads Anthony's marriage imperative through Edelman's reproductive futurity, framing his desire for Kate as a swerve away from the heteronormative dynastic mandate

concept_purpose: Ahmed's queer phenomenology of orientation, lines and the figure of the 'unhappy queer' that is disoriented by and from heteronormative paths
paper_title: Straight Time and Queer Utopia: Anthony Bridgerton and Kate Sharma's Disorientating Desire in the Regency
journal: Journal of Popular Film and Television
paper_argument: Uses Ahmed's queer orientation and 'unhappy queers' to read the couple's disorientating desire and same-sex coding before their reorientation into the heteronormative resolution

concept_purpose: Generational model of masculinities as performances that must be flexible to meet new situational demands rather than fixed 'winner-takes-all' norms
paper_title: Measures of Success: Competing Masculinities in Cobra Kai
journal: Journal of Popular Film and Television
paper_argument: Argues Cobra Kai stages an intergenerational negotiation in which rigid Reagan-era masculine norms fail Gen Z challenges, valorising flexible over static performances of manhood

concept_purpose: A theory of 'queer cuts' in editing through which diasporic, secular subjects splice fractured identities into a queer cultural genealogy against white heteropatriarchal hegemony
paper_title: 'Fractured Moments, Contradiction, and Confusion': Identifying Queer Cuts in Diasporic Speculative Media via Everything Everywhere All at Once and Russian Doll
journal: Journal of Popular Film and Television
paper_argument: Argues that the fractured, contradictory editing ('queer cuts') of these speculative texts lets diasporic North American subjects situate themselves within a queer genealogy and renegotiate normative whiteness

concept_purpose: Framework for the structural and narrative politics of serial TV fiction and its turn toward nonlinear, complex storytelling
paper_title: The Politics of Serial television Fiction: Structural Developments, Narrative Themes, and the Nonlinear Turn
journal: Historical Journal of Film, Radio and Television
paper_argument: Maps structural developments and the 'nonlinear turn' in serial television to argue that narrative form itself carries political meaning across contemporary serial drama

concept_purpose: Critical-race reading of desire and othering across species/racial coding in popular franchise media
paper_title: I'd just as soon kiss a wookiee: Uncovering racialized desire in the Star Wars galaxy
journal: Historical Journal of Film, Radio and Television
paper_argument: Uncovers how the Star Wars galaxy encodes racialized desire and othering, reading interspecies attraction and alien coding as displaced expressions of racial fantasy

concept_purpose: Mbembe's power over life and death applied to authoritarian fatherhood and patriarchal violence in Latin American cinema
paper_title: Fathers, Masculinity, and Authoritarianism in Latin American Cinema
journal: Historical Journal of Film, Radio and Television
paper_argument: Examines how Latin American films link paternal authority, masculinity and political authoritarianism, reading the father as a figure of sovereign and patriarchal power

concept_purpose: Framework of transnational co-production politics analysing how Franco-Japanese collaboration negotiates cultural particularity and postwar geopolitics
paper_title: A risky venture: Typhoon Over Nagasaki and the particularity of Franco-Japanese cinematic co-production
journal: Historical Journal of Film, Radio and Television
paper_argument: Uses the case of a Franco-Japanese co-production to theorise the cultural and industrial particularity of transnational collaboration in the postwar period

concept_purpose: Historical reception framework theorising female spectatorial pleasure, morality and faith as structuring early cinema audiences
paper_title: 'I want to be good:' morality, faith, and female spectatorial pleasure during World War I
journal: New Review of Film and Television Studies
paper_argument: Reconstructs how WWI-era female spectators derived moral and devotional pleasure from cinema, theorising spectatorship as a gendered, faith-inflected mode of engagement

concept_purpose: Banet-Weiser's concept of popular feminism as highly visible, market-friendly feminism that circulates in media economies
paper_title: Reese Witherspoon's popular feminism: adaptation and authorship in Big Little Lies
journal: New Review of Film and Television Studies
paper_argument: Analyses Witherspoon's authorship and adaptation strategy in Big Little Lies as an instance of popular feminism, where female-led production reconciles feminist visibility with commercial branding

concept_purpose: Framework theorising true-crime adaptation and feminist authorship in the #MeToo conjuncture of gendered violence and survivor testimony
paper_title: I'll Be Gone in the Dark: feminism and the adaptation of true crime in the #MeToo era
journal: New Review of Film and Television Studies
paper_argument: Argues the adaptation reframes true crime through a #MeToo-era feminist lens, centring survivor knowledge and women's investigative labour against the genre's voyeurism

concept_purpose: Affect/queer framework linking ecological precarity and intimate care to read slow, attentive tending of bodies and environments
paper_title: Flowers, concrete, water: care and precarity in Tsai Ming-liang's I Don't Want to Sleep Alone (2006)
journal: New Review of Film and Television Studies
paper_argument: Reads Tsai's film through care and precarity, arguing its attention to flowers, concrete and water stages an ethics of tending amid migrant and ecological vulnerability

concept_purpose: Munoz's disidentification: how minoritarian subjects work on and against dominant ideology, neither assimilating nor opposing but transforming it
paper_title: Girls gone wild: animality, female teenagers, and disidentification in contemporary European cinema
journal: New Review of Film and Television Studies
paper_argument: Uses Munoz's disidentification to read animal imagery and female adolescence in European cinema as a strategy by which teenage girls rework gendered and species norms

concept_purpose: Gendered framework of radicalization theorising how popular drama figures female recruits as 'lost souls, victims and deviants'
paper_title: Lost souls, victims and deviants: radicalization and gender in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.
journal: New Review of Film and Television Studies
paper_argument: Analyses how the series genders narratives of radicalization, casting women drawn into extremism as victims or deviants and thereby reproducing anxieties about female political agency

concept_purpose: A film-philosophy framework theorising the 'cinemakeover' as a transformational ethics through which films reshape the spectator's mode of being
paper_title: Transformational ethics of film: thinking the cinemakeover in the film-philosophy debate
journal: New Review of Film and Television Studies
paper_argument: Intervenes in the film-philosophy debate to argue that film enacts a transformational ('cinemakeover') ethics, reshaping how spectators perceive and live rather than merely illustrating arguments

concept_purpose: Framework linking architectural dystopia and historicity to read built environments as carriers of political-temporal meaning in speculative film
paper_title: Futures past and present: history, architecture and dystopia in Brazil (1985) and the Hunger Games series (2012-15)
journal: New Review of Film and Television Studies
paper_argument: Reads dystopian architecture in Brazil and The Hunger Games as a historicising device, arguing built space encodes anxieties about authoritarian futures rooted in the past
